institutions.name: the Temple District
institutions.title: High Priest
institutions.blurb: The temple and the shrines around it, with their almshouses, pilgrims' hostels and processions. The council decides which god's house gets the best ground and the council's coin, and that god's blessing falls on the town.

choice.label: which god the district honours first
choice.text: Whichever god gets the best ground and the council's coin blesses the town in its own way.

options.name: the Lantern Mother's healers
options.text: Her infirmary opens beside the temple: heroes come home from the wilds and are on their feet in days.

options.name: Sylvaine's harvest rites
options.text: Her priests walk the furrows each dawn: the fields and herb beds bear more.

options.name: Haldor's forge-chapel
options.text: The Anvil-Father's priests bless every hammer in town: tools come truer and buildings go up faster.

options.name: Ostrava's watch-chapel
options.text: Her priests bless the walls and the watch every dusk: the town is harder to take.

options.name: Nim's counting-house shrine
options.text: Merchants leave coins in Nim's bowl for luck, and the luck seems to stick: trade is good.

keepers.name: Ilse Varrow
keepers.text: A battlefield surgeon before she took vows, she still keeps a bone saw on the altar and has no patience for sermons.

keepers.name: Tobin Ashgrove
keepers.text: Round, kind and endlessly in debt to the temple's cook, he knows every widow in town by name and every miser by his excuses.

keepers.name: Mere Hollin
keepers.text: Blind since a fever in her girlhood, she hears confessions in the dark and says she can smell a lie.

institutions.name: the Adventurers' Hall
institutions.title: Hallmaster
institutions.blurb: Where companies register, read the contract board and gear up. Contract fees pay the town a little, and the hall's specialty shapes what its members are good for.

choice.label: what the hall is known for
choice.text: A hall gets a name for one kind of work, and draws the companies who do it.

options.name: treasure seekers
options.text: The hall takes a cut of every haul registered at its counter, and the council takes a cut of the hall's.

options.name: monster hunters
options.text: Trophy heads go up over the door. The companies who come hunt what prowls near the walls.

options.name: road wardens
options.text: Hall members ride with the caravans: fewer are waylaid on the road.

options.name: rescuers
options.text: Hall members bring back the lost and the wounded. Heroes heal faster between delves.

keepers.name: Brask Dunmore
keepers.text: A one-handed former delver who keeps the contract board in a hand so neat no one believes he wrote it, and fines anyone who spits on his floor.

keepers.name: Yeva Quell
keepers.text: A retired scout with a ledger for a memory: she can tell you which company owes which, and who is lying about a ruin.

keepers.name: Old Corrin Tarth
keepers.text: Seventy and still sharpening other people's swords, he sends every new company out with the same advice: come back.

institutions.name: the Grand Bazaar
institutions.title: Bazaar Warden
institutions.blurb: A caravanserai with stalls for visiting merchants and lodging for their beasts. The town can run one more trade route, and the warden decides which far-off traders get the best pitches.

choice.label: which merchants the bazaar invites
choice.text: There are only so many pitches under the awnings, and each kind of trader brings its own crowd.

options.name: weavers of enchanted silks
options.text: Bolts of cloth that never fade: the gentry flock, and the looms in town learn their tricks.

options.name: dealers in rare metals
options.text: Ingots from the deep holds: the smiths make better tools.

options.name: spice and incense caravans
options.text: The streets smell of far lands, and travellers come to see what the fuss is about.

options.name: sellers of monster eggs and curios
options.text: Strange cages and stranger buyers. It pays well, and the Quiet Hand takes a keen interest.

keepers.name: Saffi Delacorte
keepers.text: A merchant prince's daughter who ran away to the caravan roads, she haggles in six tongues and never pays the first price for anything.

keepers.name: Umar Kesh
keepers.text: A former caravan master with a ruined knee, he still rises before dawn to count the camels in and knows every road by its bandits.

keepers.name: Goodwife Pell Ambry
keepers.text: Once a market-wife in the old town, she rules the bazaar like a kitchen: loud, fair, and with a ladle within reach.

institutions.name: the Druid Grove
institutions.title: Grove Warden
institutions.blurb: A patch of living wilderness inside the town: an ancient tree, a sacred pool and the druids who tend them. The fields bear more, the air is sweeter, and the grove has its own opinions.

choice.label: what the grove's druids tend first
choice.text: There are few druids and much to do: the council asks them to put one thing first.

options.name: the fields
options.text: The druids walk the furrows and the orchards: the harvest is richer.

options.name: healing plants
options.text: Herb beds spread through the grove: remedies are plentiful and wounds close faster.

options.name: speaking with the wild
options.text: The druids parley with the spirits of the woods around the town: the wilds are a little less hostile.

options.name: the waters
options.text: The streams through town run clean and cold: people are healthier, and settlers notice.

keepers.name: Wren Alderhusk
keepers.text: A druid who speaks to people as if they were slow-growing trees: kindly, patiently, and with no expectation they will understand.

keepers.name: Mossback Tull
keepers.text: Nobody is sure how old he is. He sleeps in the roots of the great tree and wakes when someone drops litter.

keepers.name: Teodora Fernlight
keepers.text: Young, fierce and newly sworn to the grove, she argues with the council as if every felled tree were a personal insult, which it is.

institutions.name: the town's famous tavern
institutions.title: Proprietor
institutions.blurb: The oldest tavern in town, grown famous: where rumours land, companies form and odd visitors come asking for help. Its style decides who drinks there.

choice.label: what kind of house the tavern keeps
choice.text: A tavern can be one thing well. The council's licence says which.

options.name: a comfortable inn for travellers
options.text: Feather beds and clean linen: merchants and wealthy travellers stay, and spend.

options.name: a rowdy adventurers' pub
options.text: Arm wrestling, war stories and a wall of notices: more heroes stop in town, and some stay.

options.name: a mysterious house for strange folk
options.text: Hooded guests, low lamps and a door that is never quite locked: the Quiet Hand drinks here, and so do stranger things.

keepers.name: Marta Kettleby
keepers.text: Three husbands buried, two taverns burned and one standing: she pours with one hand and holds a cudgel with the other.

keepers.name: Fenwick Brae
keepers.text: A failed bard who learned that people pay better to talk than to listen, he remembers every story told at his bar and sells the best ones back.

keepers.name: Hobb Underbough
keepers.text: A halfling with a laugh you can hear from the gate, who has never once been seen to sleep, and keeps a book of debts he never collects.

institutions.name: the Paladin Chapterhouse
institutions.title: Knight-Commander
institutions.blurb: A fortified hall where an order of paladins keeps its vigil, trains its squires and judges its own. Its oath shapes what the knights do for the town, and a knight who breaks it is the town's problem too.

choice.label: the oath the chapter swears
choice.text: Every chapter swears one oath above the others, and the town lives with what it means.

options.name: the oath of devotion
options.text: The knights tend the sick and walk the night streets with lanterns: wounds heal and folk sleep easier.

options.name: the oath of vengeance
options.text: The knights swear to hunt every raider to its den: the wilds fear the town a little more.

options.name: the oath of the green
options.text: The knights guard the fields and orchards as if they were shrines: the harvest is safer and sweeter.

options.name: the oath of the crown
options.text: The knights swear to the town's law before their own conscience: the streets are orderly, if stern.

keepers.name: Dame Aveline Thorne
keepers.text: Forty years in the saddle and three horses buried, she still rises at the third bell to pray and expects her knights to do the same.

keepers.name: Ser Corwin Halloway
keepers.text: A reformed sellsword who found his god in a burning village, he is gentle with the weak and terrifying to everyone else.

keepers.name: Brother-Captain Joss Mallory
keepers.text: Young for his rank and painfully earnest, he keeps a ledger of every promise the town has ever made him.

institutions.name: the Alchemists' Quarter
institutions.title: Master Alchemist
institutions.blurb: A crooked lane of stills, kilns and coloured smoke where alchemists brew for the town. Potions and dyes flow out; now and then so does something that was meant to stay in the jar.

choice.label: what the quarter brews most
choice.text: Every still in the quarter can brew anything, given time. The council's coin decides what they brew first.

options.name: healing draughts
options.text: Red bottles by the crate: heroes come home sooner and fewer die of their wounds.

options.name: alchemist's fire
options.text: Clay pots of sticky flame stacked by the walls: the watch has something to throw.

options.name: dyes and perfumes
options.text: Madder reds and saffron yellows: the weavers' cloth sells further and dearer.

options.name: elixirs of youth
options.text: Very expensive, very popular and very slightly poisonous: the gold pours in.

keepers.name: Odo Brimwick
keepers.text: Eyebrowless since an accident he will not discuss, he tastes every batch himself and has outlived two apprentices who did not.

keepers.name: Sabeth Quill
keepers.text: She left the wizards' college over a matter of principle and a small fire, and has been proving them wrong ever since.

keepers.name: Old Mother Tansy
keepers.text: A herb-wife who learned her letters at sixty, she keeps her formulae in rhymes and her coin under a loose brick.

institutions.name: the Artificers' Foundry
institutions.title: Forgemaster
institutions.blurb: Furnaces, lathes and a great water-wheel, where artificers build clockwork, engines and the odd marvel. Better tools and faster building, and inventions with minds of their own.

choice.label: what the foundry builds
choice.text: The artificers can build anything the council can pay for. What they build first shapes the town.

options.name: clockwork labourers
options.text: Brass porters and stone-lifting engines: every building in town goes up faster.

options.name: engines of war
options.text: Ballistae on the towers and a springal at the gate: the walls bite back.

options.name: lamps and pumps
options.text: Clockwork pumps and everburning lamps in every street: life is easier and the nights brighter.

options.name: wonders for sale
options.text: Singing birds of silver and self-turning spits for rich men's kitchens: the merchants pay handsomely.

keepers.name: Ingra Coppervein
keepers.text: A dwarf who left her clan's forges for wanting to build things that move, she talks to her machines and claims they listen.

keepers.name: Pell Fennimore
keepers.text: A gnome of boundless enthusiasm and very few finished projects, he has patented the same kettle three times.

keepers.name: Master Hollis Grane
keepers.text: Grey, precise and humourless, he lost a hand to a steam valve and replaced it with a better one.

institutions.name: the Grand Arena
institutions.title: Arena Master
institutions.blurb: The city's arena under a master of games: duels, beasts and races before roaring crowds. It keeps the city cheerful and its coffers full, and every so often someone wants to fight to the death.

choice.label: what fills the arena
choice.text: The crowds come for anything bloody or fast. The council decides which.

options.name: heroes' duels
options.text: The town's champions spar for glory: travellers come to see a real hero fight.

options.name: beast fights
options.text: Owlbears and bulettes dragged from the wilds and killed before the crowd: the wilds seem less fearsome.

options.name: chariot races
options.text: Four teams, four colours, and wagers on all of them: a river of gold.

options.name: trials by combat
options.text: Grudges settled with blunted blades instead of knives in alleys: the streets are calmer.

keepers.name: Varro Stake
keepers.text: A retired gladiator with a voice like a landslide, he knows every fighter's weakness and every bookmaker's price.

keepers.name: Lady Ismene Corr
keepers.text: A noblewoman who bought the games to annoy her family, she runs them with a fan in one hand and a ledger in the other.

keepers.name: Grumm One-Tusk
keepers.text: A half-orc who fought in the pits as a boy, he insists every fighter is paid and every beast is fed.

institutions.name: the Bards' College
institutions.title: Dean of Bards
institutions.blurb: The theatre becomes a college of bards: players, poets and loremasters who sing the town's deeds and keep its memory. What they sing about decides how the town sees itself, and what the world hears of it.

choice.label: what the college sings
choice.text: Bards will sing anything. The town will believe what they sing most.

options.name: the deeds of the town's heroes
options.text: Ballads of every delve and duel: heroes walk taller, and more come looking for the town in the songs.

options.name: the old histories
options.text: Lays of the fallen kingdoms: the town's scholars learn faster, and its people know their place in the world.

options.name: satires of the powerful
options.text: Nobody is safe from the stage, the mayor least of all: folk laugh instead of riot.

options.name: songs of love
options.text: Every tavern hums the season's tune: the town is a happier place to live.

keepers.name: Lysander Vale
keepers.text: Once the most famous voice in the Free Ports, now hoarse and vain, he teaches as if every pupil were his last chance at an encore.

keepers.name: Mistress Oona Fairweather
keepers.text: A halfling loremaster who has memorised four thousand verses and forgives no one a wrong rhyme.

keepers.name: Kit Marlow
keepers.text: A young playwright with a quill sharper than most swords and enemies in every guildhall.

fixtures.name: a mimic for a bouncer
fixtures.text: A young mimic sits by the tavern door as a strongbox. Troublemakers who sit on it once never come back.

fixtures.name: a mimic strongbox
fixtures.text: The hall's strongbox has teeth. Nothing has been stolen since.

fixtures.name: a temple's guardian chest
fixtures.text: A mimic, blessed and fed on offerings, guards the reliquary. The priests say it purrs at hymns.

fixtures.name: the living bridge
fixtures.text: Willow and ash grown into a bridge over the river. Carts cross it, children climb it, and it grows a little every spring.

fixtures.name: the pilgrims' hostel
fixtures.text: A long hall of cots beside the temple for those who walk to it. Some stay.

fixtures.name: the oak in the square
fixtures.text: The awakened oak that walked to the market square, and stayed. It shades the stalls and settles arguments by dropping acorns.

fixtures.name: the trophy wall
fixtures.text: Heads, horns and a manticore's tail over the hall's hearth. Young heroes come to see it.

fixtures.name: the spice garden
fixtures.text: Seeds from a far caravan, coaxed into a walled garden behind the bazaar. Its pepper sells for silver.

fixtures.name: the oath-stone
fixtures.text: A standing stone in the chapterhouse yard where the town's oaths are sworn. Few lie with a hand on it.

fixtures.name: everburning lamps
fixtures.text: Glass globes of cold alchemical light along the main street, gifts of a grateful quarter.

fixtures.name: the brass gatekeeper
fixtures.text: A clockwork sentinel at the gate that never sleeps and never takes a bribe.

fixtures.name: the champion's statue
fixtures.text: A bronze of the town's greatest arena champion, polished bright by the hands of every child who touches it for luck.

fixtures.name: the town's anthem
fixtures.text: A song written for the town that every child knows by heart and every traveller carries away.

precedents.text: The town promised the grove the river would run clean
The town broke its promise to keep the river clean
The Quiet Hand was given a stall in the bazaar's back rows
The town gave a fallen knight a second chance
The town licenses every invention the foundry builds
The town promised its bards they may mock anyone

stages.text: Forty pilgrims have walked to {institution} for the holy day, footsore and with nowhere to sleep. {keeper} asks the town to shelter them.

success.text: The council pays for a long hall of cots beside the temple. The pilgrims bless the town on their way home, and some never leave.

options.label: Ask the faithful to take them in

success.text: Spare rooms open all over town. The pilgrims go home full of the town's kindness.

failure.text: Doors stay shut. The pilgrims sleep in the temple porch, and {keeperName} sleeps beside them in protest.

success.text: The pilgrims trudge on to another town. {keeperName} does not speak to the council for a week.

ignored.text: No one decides, and the pilgrims sleep in the street.

stages.text: The reliquary of {institution} has been forced in the night and its holiest relic is gone. {keeper} is beside themself, and {hero} has offered to help.

success.text: {heroName} tracks the thieves to a barge on the river and brings the relic home in triumph.

failure.text: The trail goes cold at the river. {heroName} comes back empty-handed and embarrassed.

options.label: Quietly buy it back from the Quiet Hand

success.text: A knock at midnight, a purse changes hands, and the relic is on the altar by dawn. Nobody asks how.

options.label: Have the priests pray for its return

success.text: Three days of vigil, and the relic is found on the temple steps, the thief weeping beside it.

failure.text: The vigil ends with nothing but sore knees.

ignored.text: The relic is never found. The faithful say the town did not care.

stages.text: {keeper} wants the town to keep the high holy day of {institution} with a procession, bonfires and a feast in the square.

success.text: Banners, music and roast oxen. The whole town turns out and the priests are hoarse with blessing.
Bread, ale and a short procession. Everyone enjoys it, briefly.
{keeperName} agrees the treasury has better uses this year, and almost means it.

failure.text: {keeperName} leaves the council chamber white with anger.

ignored.text: The holy day passes with no feast, and the faithful notice.

requests.title: A holy well in the way

stages.text: Builders digging new foundations have struck an old holy well, sealed long ago. {keeper} wants work stopped and the well kept.

options.label: Keep the well and build around it

success.text: The well is cleaned and roofed. Townsfolk drink from it for luck.
The well is filled in. The builders finish early, and {keeperName} calls it sacrilege from the pulpit.

options.label: Find the old rite to move its blessing

success.text: {keeperName} finds the words in an old book, and the blessing moves to the temple font. Everyone is satisfied.

failure.text: The rite goes wrong, the well floods the site and the builders down tools.

ignored.text: The argument drags on until the builders fill the well in anyway.

stages.text: {keeper} has {hero} free this week and two jobs on the slate: a look at {site}, or riding guard on the caravan road to {settlement}.

success.text: {heroName} comes back with a sketch map and a fistful of old coins. The way into {site} is known now.
The caravan gets through without a scratch, and {people} remember who sent the guard.
{heroName} scouts {site} by night and rides with the caravan by day, and pulls it off.

failure.text: Trying to be in two places at once, {heroName} manages neither well and comes home bloodied.

ignored.text: The week goes by and {heroName} drinks it away at the hall.

stages.text: {hero}'s company and another have been at each other's throats over who cleared a ruin first. {keeper} wants the mayor to settle it before somebody is stabbed in the hall.

options.label: Make them race for the next bounty

success.text: Both companies sprint for the hills. The rivalry becomes the town's favourite sport.

failure.text: The race turns into a brawl on the north road.

success.text: A sharp word, a heavy fine, and peace returns.

failure.text: Nobody listens, and {keeperName} has to break up the fight with a chair.

options.label: Let them settle it in the yard

success.text: A bout in the hall's yard, cheered by half the town. {heroName} wins, bruised.

ignored.text: The quarrel festers, and both companies drink elsewhere for a while.

stages.text: {hero}'s company came home with gold, monster hide and a complication: an envoy of {people} at the hall's door, saying the ruin they looted was a burial ground of their ancestors.

success.text: Coin and an apology. {people} go home mollified.
The council says finders keepers. {heroName} is grateful; {people} are not.

options.label: Broker a ceremony to return what matters

success.text: The bones go home with honour, the gold stays. Everyone leaves satisfied.

failure.text: The talks collapse in shouting.

ignored.text: Nobody answers the envoy, who leaves in a cold fury.

stages.text: {party} are a week overdue. {keeper} wants to send a rescue company after them and asks the council to pay for it.

success.text: The rescuers find {party} holed up in a cave, hungry but alive, and bring them home to cheers.
A voice crackles back from the wilds: they are pinned down but holding. The hall breathes again.

failure.text: The stone stays silent. {keeperName} paces all night.

success.text: The council says so. {keeperName} says something worse.

ignored.text: No one goes. {party} will make it home or they won't.

stages.text: A trader in a fur hood has set up at {institution} with a crate of warm, speckled eggs. {keeper} wants to know whether the town will allow it.

options.label: Buy the clutch and sell the hatchlings on

success.text: The hatchlings fetch a fortune from a noble's menagerie.

failure.text: The eggs hatch early in the warehouse. It takes the watch two days to catch everything.

options.label: Let the trader sell, for a licence fee

success.text: A brisk trade in eggs, and a fat licence for the treasury.
The crate goes back on the cart. {keeperName} sighs at the lost fee.

ignored.text: The trader sells the eggs anyway, to whoever asks.

stages.text: Two caravans want the town's guard on the same road: a spice train bound for {institution}, and the town's own convoy to {settlement}. There are only enough riders for one.

success.text: The spices arrive safe and the bazaar does a week's trade in a day.
The convoy gets through. {people} are pleased; {keeperName} is not.
Both get through, and the sellswords drink their pay at the bazaar.

ignored.text: Both caravans set out without guards and hope for the best.

stages.text: A soft-spoken woman from {faction} says they know of a smuggling ring working out of {institution}. They will name names, in exchange for a stall in the bazaar's restricted back rows.

success.text: The smugglers are taken in a night. The Hand gets its stall, and {keeperName} gets a new neighbour {keeperName} did not choose.

options.label: Refuse, and have the watch find the smugglers

success.text: Two weeks of patient watching, and the ring is broken without the Hand's help.

failure.text: The smugglers get wind of the watch and slip away.

options.label: Tell {keeperName} and let the bazaar deal with it

success.text: {keeperName} thanks the mayor, and the bazaar's porters see the smugglers out of town.

failure.text: {keeperName} thinks the mayor is accusing the bazaar, and takes offence.

ignored.text: The offer is withdrawn, and the smuggling goes on.

stages.text: A caravan from the far oasis cities has brought a chest of old books to {institution}: star charts, bestiaries, a grimoire with a lock on it. {keeper} has kept them back for the town to see first.

options.label: Buy them for the town's scholars

success.text: The books go to the town's shelves. The mayor reads late into the night, and learns something.

options.label: Let the Order of the Unshut Book bid

success.text: The Order outbids everyone and is delighted. The bazaar takes its cut.

options.label: Have someone open the grimoire first

success.text: The lock gives, and the grimoire holds nothing worse than an alchemist's recipes. It sells for a good price.

failure.text: Something comes out of the grimoire, and it takes the town's priests a day to put it back.

ignored.text: The books are sold off a cart to whoever asks.

stages.text: The tanneries upstream are fouling the stream that feeds the grove's sacred pool. {keeper} wants them moved downstream.

success.text: New pits downstream, and the pool runs clear again.

options.label: Fine the tanners into cleaning up

success.text: The tanners grumble, pay and dig settling ponds.

failure.text: The tanners laugh at the fine and carry on.

options.label: Tell the druids to live with it

success.text: The pool scums over. The druids say nothing, which is worse.

ignored.text: The stream stays foul and the pool sickens.

stages.text: The grove's oldest oak has woken and decided to move. It wants to stand in the market square, and is already halfway down the lane. {keeper} asks the mayor to clear it a way.

options.label: Clear it a path to the square

success.text: Stalls are moved and a wall comes down. The oak settles in the square with a long creak of contentment.

options.label: Persuade it to stay in the grove

success.text: A long, slow conversation at dawn. The oak agrees to stay, for another hundred years.

failure.text: The oak does not care for being argued with, and walks through the tanners' yard instead.

success.text: Chains and posts. The oak stops, and the grove goes very quiet.

ignored.text: The oak walks where it likes, and the town picks up the pieces.

stages.text: {keeper} offers to grow a living bridge of willow and ash across the river, on one condition: the river beneath it must be kept clean forever.

success.text: The druids sing to the saplings, and in a season a bridge stands where none did.

options.label: Ask for a bridge without promises

success.text: {keeperName} considers it and agrees, on a smaller bridge.

failure.text: {keeperName} says a gift with no promise is a purchase, and the grove does not sell.

success.text: The council builds its own bridge of stone, later and dearer.

ignored.text: The offer withers on the bough.

stages.text: A dyer's vat has burst and the river below the living bridge runs blue. {keeper} reminds the mayor of the town's promise.

options.label: Pay for the river to be cleaned

success.text: Men with nets and buckets work for a week, and the river runs clear. The bridge puts out new leaves.
The dyer pays, and the river is cleaned.

failure.text: The dyer has nothing to pay with, and the river stays blue.

success.text: The bridge withers on one side. The druids say the town's word is worth nothing.

ignored.text: No one cleans it up. The promise is broken.

stages.text: The spirits of the woods beyond the walls are furious with the woodcutters. Wolves follow the timber carts, and trees fall across the roads. {keeper} offers to parley for the town.

success.text: The spirits accept a bargain: the woodcutters plant two for every one they fell.

failure.text: The spirits will not listen, and the woods grow darker.

success.text: The woodcutters work fewer days and the woods settle.
Wolves hang from the gate, and the grove's druids weep.

ignored.text: The woods stay angry.

stages.text: {hero} would hang up the sword and buy a share of {institution} from {keeper}. There is a catch: old enemies have a way of following a hero to their door.

success.text: {heroName} buys in and pulls pints between delves. Business booms.
{heroName} agrees the wilds still need them, and stays on the road.

failure.text: {heroName} sulks for a week.

stages.text: A month later, a band of hard-faced strangers walks into {institution} and asks for {heroName} by an old name.

success.text: {heroName} meets them in the yard, and the strangers leave on stretchers. The tavern's fame doubles.

failure.text: The fight wrecks the taproom, and {heroName} is badly hurt.

success.text: A heavy purse and they ride away, promising nothing.
The watch takes them in before a blow is struck.

failure.text: The watch arrives late, to a broken taproom.

ignored.text: The strangers wait for {heroName} in the street, and it ends in blood.
{heroName} takes the silence as a no.

stages.text: A cloaked stranger has sat in the corner of {institution} for three nights, asking anyone who will listen for help with something buried at {site}. {keeper} thinks the mayor should hear it.

success.text: The stranger draws a map on the table in spilled ale and is gone by morning. The map is good.

failure.text: The stranger talks in riddles and leaves without paying.

success.text: A purse for a parchment. The map is old, but good.
{keeperName} does it, unhappily.

ignored.text: The stranger leaves town, and takes the story with them.

stages.text: {hero}'s company carried home a magnificent treasure chest. In the hall's strongroom it bit the clerk. It is a young mimic, and everyone in town has an idea what to do with it.

options.label: Give it to the tavern as a bouncer

success.text: The mimic takes to its new door at once. Brawls at the tavern end very quickly now.

options.label: Let the temple bless and keep it

success.text: Fed on offerings and hymns, the mimic guards the reliquary like a hound.

options.label: Let the Quiet Hand train it

success.text: The Hand's people take it away in a sack. Strongboxes across town start going missing, but never theirs.

options.label: Tame it as the hall's strongbox

success.text: It learns to open only for {keeperName}. The hall has never been safer.

failure.text: It does not want to be tamed, and {heroName} loses a fingertip finding out.

ignored.text: Nobody decides, and one morning the mimic is gone, along with a cartwheel.

stages.text: The priests of {institution2} want a bough of the grove's ancient tree for a new altar. {keeper} refuses: you do not cut a living elder to carve a dead one. Both come to the mayor.

success.text: The tree keeps its bough. The priests find oak elsewhere, sourly.
The bough is cut with great ceremony. The druids watch in silence.
The tree lets fall a bough of its own accord at a joint dawn rite. Both call it a miracle.

failure.text: The rite turns into a shouting match under the tree.

ignored.text: The quarrel rumbles on, and both blame the mayor.

stages.text: {hero} wants to sell a jewelled idol from the wilds at {institution2}. {keeper2} wants the bazaar's cut; {keeper} insists the hall's fee comes first. The idol sits on the council table between them.

success.text: The hall takes its fee and the bazaar sulks.

options.label: The bazaar sells it, the bazaar's cut

success.text: The bazaar takes its cut and the hall grumbles.
A public auction draws half the region. The idol fetches a fortune, and both keepers are paid.

failure.text: The auction draws thieves as well as buyers, and the idol vanishes in the crush.

ignored.text: {hero} sells it to a passing pedlar for half its worth.

stages.text: {hero}'s new ballad about the companies of {institution} is sung in every tavern on the road. Recruits are arriving, and so are challengers who want to test the town's heroes.

success.text: The ballad spreads. New faces fill the hall, and a few bloody noses with them.

options.label: Ask for a verse about the town

success.text: {heroName} adds three verses about the town's walls and warm beds. Settlers come, not just swords.

failure.text: The new verses rhyme 'town' with 'drown'. Nobody sings them.

success.text: {heroName} is hurt, but sings something else.

ignored.text: The ballad goes where ballads go.

stages.text: {keeper} has noticed {faction} meeting in the back room of {institution} every Moonday, and wants to know whether the mayor would rather they did or didn't.

options.label: Let them meet there, and listen

success.text: {keeperName} keeps an ear to the wall. The town learns a great deal.

options.label: Let them meet, and leave them be

success.text: The Hand notices the courtesy.
{keeperName} turns them out with a smile and a cudgel.

failure.text: The Hand turns {keeperName}'s cellar out first. Barrels are broken.

ignored.text: The Hand keeps meeting, and nobody says anything.

stages.text: One of {keeper}'s knights got drunk, drew steel on a carter and broke {choice}. The chapter would strip him of his spurs and drive him out; his family begs the mayor for mercy.

options.label: Let the chapter judge its own

success.text: The knight rides out of the gate at dawn without his spurs. The chapter is satisfied.
{keeperName} grants it, grudgingly: the knight will serve a year as a squire again.

failure.text: {keeperName} will not hear of it, and resents being asked.

options.label: Have the town's court try him instead

success.text: The court fines him and lets him go. The knights mutter about civil men judging holy ones.

ignored.text: The chapter judges him without the mayor, and notes that the mayor did not care.

stages.text: {keeper} asks the council's blessing and purse for a crusade against {menace}. The knights would ride out within the week.

success.text: The knights ride out under the town's banner and return with {menace} bloodied and their ranks thinned.
The knights go anyway, fewer and poorer, and do what they can.

failure.text: Without coin the crusade never leaves the yard, and the knights blame the council.

options.label: Forbid it: the town needs them here

success.text: The knights stay and stand on the walls, sullen.

ignored.text: The knights wait for a blessing that never comes.

stages.text: {keeper} wants the great square for the chapter's vigil on the same night {keeper2} has promised it to the temple's procession. Both expect the mayor to settle it.

options.label: Give the square to the knights

success.text: The vigil is splendid, and the priests sulk in the side streets.

options.label: Give the square to the temple

success.text: The procession is glorious, and the knights stand guard at its edges, stone-faced.
Knights and priests keep the night together, and it becomes a festival the town remembers.

failure.text: Knights and priests spend the night arguing over precedence in front of everyone.

ignored.text: Both turn up, and the night ends with shoving.

stages.text: A still in {institution} has gone up in green fire and taken a neighbour's roof with it. The neighbours want the quarter moved outside the walls; {keeper} says it was an accident and will not happen again.

options.label: Pay for the roof and let them carry on

success.text: A new roof, a stern word, and the quarter goes back to work.
{keeperName} pays, with very bad grace.

options.label: Order stone walls between the stills

success.text: The quarter grumbles and builds them. Nothing has burned since.

ignored.text: The neighbours take the matter into their own hands, and the quarter's windows are broken.

stages.text: {keeper} needs the heart of a beast from {site} for a great work, and offers the council a share of what comes of it.

success.text: The heart arrives in a bucket of ice, and the quarter's great work bubbles for a month.
{keeperName} goes, and comes back singed but triumphant.

failure.text: {keeperName} comes back without it, and without an eyebrow.

success.text: The great work waits.

ignored.text: The great work waits.

stages.text: The alchemists want to harvest the moonpetal that grows only in the druids' sacred pool. {keeper} offers good coin; {keeper2} says the pool is not for sale.

success.text: The moonpetal stays. The alchemists find a substitute that works almost as well.
The petals are harvested, the potions are superb, and the druids do not forgive it.
The druids harvest a few petals each full moon, and sell them dear. Both sides are grudgingly content.

failure.text: Neither side will budge, and both blame the mayor.

ignored.text: The alchemists harvest by night, and the druids catch them at it.

stages.text: One of {keeper}'s clockwork labourers has wandered out of {institution} and is carrying a market stall, very carefully, towards the river.

options.label: Send the watch to stop it

success.text: Six watchmen and a net bring it down. The stall survives; the watchmen are bruised.

failure.text: The automaton walks into the river, stall and all. The stallholder wants paying.

success.text: {keeperName} whistles a long, odd tune, and it puts the stall down and walks home.

failure.text: {keeperName}'s tune makes it walk faster.

success.text: Hammers make short work of it. {keeperName} weeps over the parts.

ignored.text: The automaton reaches the river and keeps walking. It is still down there.

stages.text: Two of the foundry's artificers swear they invented the same self-stoking furnace. {keeper} wants the council to grant one a licence and settle it.

options.label: Grant licences on the council's terms

success.text: From now on, every invention is licensed by the town, for a fee. The artificers grumble and pay.
They hate each other, and the furnace is the best ever built.

failure.text: They burn the first one down arguing over the flue.

success.text: {keeperName} settles it by giving the furnace to a third artificer entirely.

ignored.text: The quarrel goes on for months.

stages.text: {keeper} has learned that the town's library holds a dwarven book of schematics, and wants it lent to the foundry. The librarians say it is far too old to leave the reading room.

success.text: The schematics come back oily and dog-eared, and the foundry builds something marvellous from them.
A careful copy goes to the foundry; the original stays safe. The gatekeeper they build from it stands at the gate to this day.
The book stays where it is. {keeperName} is not pleased.

ignored.text: {keeperName} tries to borrow it without asking, and is caught.

stages.text: A champion from the south has beaten every fighter in {institution} and now calls out {hero} by name before the whole crowd. {keeper} says the town's honour is on the line.

success.text: {heroName} wins in the fourth bout, and the crowd carries them through the streets.

failure.text: {heroName} loses badly and limps off to jeers.

success.text: The crowd boos, and {keeperName} has to give back half the gate.
The fight is thrilling and the result never in doubt. Only {keeperName} knows.

ignored.text: The southern champion claims the town has no heroes, and the crowd half believes it.

requests.title: A beast loose from the pens

stages.text: An owlbear has broken out of the arena's pens and is loose in the streets. {keeper} swears the bars were sound.

success.text: The watch corners it in a bakery, with losses on both sides.

failure.text: The watch flees, and the owlbear eats the bakery's stock and goes back to its pen of its own accord.

success.text: {heroName} drives it back into the pen with a torch and a lot of shouting.

failure.text: {heroName} is mauled, and the beast is killed.

options.label: Close the arena's pens for good

success.text: No more beasts in the arena. The crowds are smaller.

ignored.text: The owlbear rampages for a night before the watch kills it.

stages.text: The college's new play is about a vain, greedy mayor who looks remarkably like the real one. The town loves it. {keeper} waits to see what the mayor will do.

success.text: The mayor attends opening night and laughs loudest. The town warms to them.

options.label: Ask for the worst lines to be cut

success.text: {keeperName} cuts them, and the cut lines become the town's favourite jokes.

failure.text: {keeperName} refuses, loudly, on stage.

success.text: The play closes. Everyone hears about it, and everyone takes the bards' side.

ignored.text: The play runs for months, and nobody hears the mayor's side.

stages.text: {keeper} wants to write the hall's great ballad, but {keeper2} insists it be about {hero} and get every detail right. The bards say the truth is never as good as the song.

success.text: The ballad is magnificent and largely invented. {heroName} is famous for things they never did.
The ballad is shorter, and the hall's companies love it.
{heroName} tells it in the taproom, and the bards scribble. The ballad is honest and stirring.

failure.text: {heroName} stammers through it, and the bards fill in the gaps.

ignored.text: The bards write it anyway, and the hall hates it.

stages.text: A travelling troupe has set up in the square and is drawing the college's crowds. {keeper} asks the council to move them on.

success.text: The troupe moves on, and the college's benches fill again.
The two companies stage a festival of plays together, and the town talks of nothing else.

failure.text: The two companies hate each other on sight.

success.text: The troupe stays a month and the college sulks.

ignored.text: The troupe stays, and the college sulks.
